    async def read_xlsx_async(
    source: XlsxSource,
    *,
    sheet: str | int = 0,
    max_rows: int | None = DEFAULT_XLSX_MAX_ROWS,
    max_uncompressed_bytes: int | None = DEFAULT_XLSX_MAX_UNCOMPRESSED_BYTES,
    max_compression_ratio: float | None = DEFAULT_XLSX_MAX_COMPRESSION_RATIO,
    semaphore: asyncio.Semaphore | None = None,
) -> list[dict[str, XlsxCellValue]]:
    """Read one tab of an ``.xlsx`` workbook without blocking the event loop.

    :func:`read_xlsx` in a worker thread, behind a semaphore. The parse is
    CPU-bound and takes seconds on a large tab, so calling the synchronous
    reader from a coroutine — an upload endpoint — stops every other
    request of the worker for that long. This is the one to ``await``.

    Args:
        source (XlsxSource): The workbook as bytes, a path, or a binary
            file object. A file object is read from the worker thread.
        sheet (str | int): The tab's name, or its 0-based position.
        max_rows (int | None): As in :func:`read_xlsx`.
        max_uncompressed_bytes (int | None): As in :func:`read_xlsx`.
        max_compression_ratio (float | None): As in :func:`read_xlsx`.
        semaphore (asyncio.Semaphore | None): Bounds how many reads run at
            once. ``None`` shares one semaphore of
            :data:`DEFAULT_MAX_CONCURRENT_XLSX_READS` per event loop.

    Returns:
        list[dict[str, XlsxCellValue]]: The data rows, in sheet order.

    Raises:
        ImportError: When the ``[spreadsheet]`` extra is not installed.
        ValueError: If a limit is zero or negative.
        SpreadsheetTooLargeError: If the workbook passes a limit.
        InvalidSpreadsheetError: If the source is not an ``.xlsx``.
        SheetNotFoundError: If the workbook has no such tab.
        FileNotFoundError: If a path does not exist.
    """
    async with _read_semaphore(semaphore):
        return await asyncio.to_thread(
            read_xlsx,
            source,
            sheet=sheet,
            max_rows=max_rows,
            max_uncompressed_bytes=max_uncompressed_bytes,
            max_compression_ratio=max_compression_ratio,
        )

    async def read_xlsx_as_async[ModelT: BaseModel](
    source: XlsxSource,
    schema: type[ModelT],
    *,
    sheet: str | int = 0,
    omit_blank: bool = True,
    max_rows: int | None = DEFAULT_XLSX_MAX_ROWS,
    max_uncompressed_bytes: int | None = DEFAULT_XLSX_MAX_UNCOMPRESSED_BYTES,
    max_compression_ratio: float | None = DEFAULT_XLSX_MAX_COMPRESSION_RATIO,
    semaphore: asyncio.Semaphore | None = None,
) -> list[ModelT]:
    """Read one tab and validate each row without blocking the event loop.

    :func:`read_xlsx_as` in a worker thread — the parse and the row
    validation both run there — behind the same semaphore as
    :func:`read_xlsx_async`.

    Args:
        source (XlsxSource): The workbook as bytes, a path, or a binary
            file object. A file object is read from the worker thread.
        schema (type[ModelT]): The Pydantic model each row validates into.
        sheet (str | int): The tab's name, or its 0-based position.
        omit_blank (bool): As in :func:`read_xlsx_as`.
        max_rows (int | None): As in :func:`read_xlsx_as`.
        max_uncompressed_bytes (int | None): As in :func:`read_xlsx_as`.
        max_compression_ratio (float | None): As in :func:`read_xlsx_as`.
        semaphore (asyncio.Semaphore | None): Bounds how many reads run at
            once. ``None`` shares one semaphore of
            :data:`DEFAULT_MAX_CONCURRENT_XLSX_READS` per event loop.

    Returns:
        list[ModelT]: One instance per data row, in sheet order.

    Raises:
        ImportError: When the ``[spreadsheet]`` extra is not installed.
        ValueError: If a limit is zero or negative.
        SpreadsheetTooLargeError: If the workbook passes a limit.
        InvalidSpreadsheetError: If the source is not an ``.xlsx``.
        SheetNotFoundError: If the workbook has no such tab.
        SpreadsheetRowError: On the first row that fails validation.
        FileNotFoundError: If a path does not exist.
    """
    async with _read_semaphore(semaphore):
        return await asyncio.to_thread(
            read_xlsx_as,
            source,
            schema,
            sheet=sheet,
            omit_blank=omit_blank,
            max_rows=max_rows,
            max_uncompressed_bytes=max_uncompressed_bytes,
            max_compression_ratio=max_compression_ratio,
        )

    """Read every tab of an ``.xlsx`` workbook without blocking the event loop.

    XlsxCellValue module-attribute ¶

    XlsxCellValue = str | int | float | bool | datetime | time | timedelta | None

    What a cell of a read .xlsx holds.

    The type openpyxl (data_only=True) hands back, unchanged:

    • a number is int or float — whichever the file wrote. The Google export writes 30.0 and 50 in the same column, so declare the field float or Decimal, not int. Currency is a plain number (84.39); a percentage is the ratio (0.4 for 40%).
    • a date is a datetime — also for a date-only cell, at midnight; a time-only cell is a time, a duration format a timedelta.
    • a formula is its cached result; a formula whose result is the empty string reads as None, like an empty cell.
    • an error cell (#DIV/0!) is its text.

    XlsxSource module-attribute ¶

    XlsxSource = bytes | str | PathLike[str] | IO[bytes]

    Where a workbook is read from.

    bytes (an upload read into memory, an HTTP body), a filesystem path, or a binary file object — UploadFile.file included.

    Bases: FileTooLargeException

    The workbook is past one of the limits the readers enforce.

    Raised before the work the limit protects: the decompressed size and the compression ratio are read from the ZIP's central directory before openpyxl opens the file, the row limit trips on the first row past it, and the download limit stops the transfer as soon as the body passes it. Nothing is truncated: a sheet over a limit is refused, never read in part.

    details["limit"] names the limit — "uncompressed_bytes", "compression_ratio", "rows" or "download_bytes" —, details["max"] its value, and details["actual"] what was found (for "rows" and "download_bytes", the count at which reading stopped). details["member"] names the ZIP member for the ratio and details["sheet"] the tab for the row limit (None for a CSV export, which carries no tab name).

    A subclass of :class:~tempest_fastapi_sdk.exceptions.FileTooLargeException, so the status is 413 like the SDK's upload limit, and except FileTooLargeException covers both.

    DEFAULT_XLSX_MAX_ROWS module-attribute ¶

    DEFAULT_XLSX_MAX_ROWS: Final[int] = 100000

    Data rows a tab may hold before the readers refuse it.

    Counted per tab, blank rows excluded, while the tab is streamed: row max_rows + 1 raises before it is kept, so the refused part of the sheet is never held in memory.

    The CSV readers of :mod:~tempest_fastapi_sdk.spreadsheet.google (read_google_sheet, read_google_sheet_as) apply the same default, counted the same way while the CSV is parsed.

    The arithmetic, measured with openpyxl 3.1.5 on CPython 3.11 (one run per size): a generated tab of 8 columns (id, two texts, three numbers, a date, a status) read by :func:read_xlsx peaked at 291.5 MB of RSS with 200 000 rows and at 959.1 MB with 1 000 000 rows — about 834 bytes per row — and took 15.6 s and 78.1 s, about 78 µs per row, on top of the ~125 MB the interpreter and the engine already hold. With this default the 200 000-row tab was refused at row 100 001 after 10.8 s, peaking at 214 MB. The real workbook measured (a public Google Sheet, 16 tabs, 2 580 rows in all) is 39 times below it.

    DEFAULT_XLSX_MAX_UNCOMPRESSED_BYTES module-attribute ¶

    DEFAULT_XLSX_MAX_UNCOMPRESSED_BYTES: Final[int] = 100 * 1024 * 1024

    Bytes the workbook's parts may add up to once decompressed (100 MiB).

    An .xlsx is a ZIP, so the size of the upload says nothing about the size the engine parses: a 1.7 MB file measured here inflates to 505 MB of sheet XML and peaked at 2 278 MB of RSS in the unguarded reader. The sum is taken from the ZIP's central directory before openpyxl opens anything.

    The arithmetic: the same 8-column tab costs ~404 bytes of sheet XML per row and ~834 bytes of RSS per row once read, so memory grows by about 2 bytes per byte of XML: a workbook right under 100 MiB holds about 215 MB of rows (estimated from that ratio, not measured). A tab of the default :data:DEFAULT_XLSX_MAX_ROWS rows in that shape is ~40 MB of XML, so for narrow sheets the row limit trips first; this one binds wide sheets, many tabs and large shared-string tables. The 16-tab Google Sheet measured is 6.1 MB decompressed.

    It also bounds time. Without a <dimension> tag — the Google export writes none — openpyxl scans the whole sheet XML when it opens the workbook, before the first row is read (a 505 MB sheet took 45.8 s). A file built to sit just under this limit, with the ratio check off, was refused at row 100 001 after 11.4 s, peaking at 248 MB: the worst case the defaults allow, as measured.

    The central directory can lie, and zipfile is what keeps the lie harmless: it stops decompressing a member at the size the directory declares and checks the CRC there (measured on CPython 3.11 to 3.14). A member that claims 4 KiB and holds 50 MB reads as 4 KiB and then fails — the CRC does not match, or the XML is cut short — and either way surfaces as :class:InvalidSpreadsheetError, never as 50 MB in memory.

    DEFAULT_XLSX_MAX_COMPRESSION_RATIO module-attribute ¶

    DEFAULT_XLSX_MAX_COMPRESSION_RATIO: Final[float] = 100.0

    Decompressed-to-compressed size a single ZIP member may reach.

    Checked on members of at least 1 MiB decompressed — a small member cannot hurt, and its ratio says little. Measured on legitimate workbooks: the sheets of the 16-tab Google Sheet compress 7.8 to 8.1 times (its worst member, styles.xml, 11.6), openpyxl output with distinct rows 7.2, and a tab of 200 000 identical rows — the most repetitive legitimate content — 14.7. A sheet XML built to inflate compressed 294.5 times, and deflate reaches about 1 032 at most. 100 leaves the legitimate files more than six times of headroom and refuses the bomb even when its total stays under :data:DEFAULT_XLSX_MAX_UNCOMPRESSED_BYTES.

    DEFAULT_MAX_CONCURRENT_XLSX_READS module-attribute ¶

    DEFAULT_MAX_CONCURRENT_XLSX_READS: Final[int] = 4

    Reads the async readers let run at once in one event loop.

    openpyxl parses in pure Python and holds the GIL, so the worker threads behind the *_async readers keep the loop answering but do not add throughput: concurrent reads share one core. What the limit bounds is memory — each read holds its whole tab, which is ~834 bytes per row by the measurement behind :data:DEFAULT_XLSX_MAX_ROWS — and the default thread pool, which the rest of the service shares. Pass your own :class:asyncio.Semaphore as semaphore to size it differently.

    def parse_slides(
    text: str,
    *,
    deck_title: str | None = None,
    vocabulary: SlideVocabulary = DEFAULT_SLIDE_VOCABULARY,
    max_chars: int | None = DEFAULT_MAX_SOURCE_CHARS,
) -> SlideDeck:
    """Parse structured text into a slide deck.

    Each lesson header opens a lesson and becomes its cover slide. Inside
    it, a short capitalized line opens a section; paragraphs and bullets
    under a section become content and bullet slides, split so none
    overflows; a section whose title contains the vocabulary's
    ``conclusion_marker`` becomes conclusion slides. Content before the
    first lesson header goes into an implicit lesson 1.

    Args:
        text (str): The source text.
        deck_title (str | None): Overrides the deck title, which is
            otherwise the first lesson's title.
        vocabulary (SlideVocabulary): Markers to recognize and labels to
            print. English by default.
        max_chars (int | None): Longest accepted source, in characters;
            ``None`` accepts any length.

    Returns:
        SlideDeck: The deck, slides numbered from 1.

    Raises:
        SlideSourceEmptyError: If ``text`` is empty or whitespace.
        SlideSourceTooLargeError: If ``text`` is longer than ``max_chars``.
    """
    _check_source(text, max_chars)
    lessons = _DeckReader(vocabulary).read(text)
    slides = _build_slides(lessons, vocabulary)
    title = deck_title or (
        lessons[0].title if lessons else vocabulary.default_deck_title
    )
    return SlideDeck(title=title, slides=slides)

    def parse_answer_key(
    text: str,
    *,
    title: str | None = None,
    subtitle: str | None = None,
    vocabulary: AnswerKeyVocabulary = DEFAULT_ANSWER_KEY_VOCABULARY,
    max_chars: int | None = DEFAULT_MAX_SOURCE_CHARS,
) -> AnswerKey:
    """Parse structured text into an answer key.

    A numbered line (``1.`` or ``1)``) opens a question; the vocabulary's
    answer marker opens its answer, which runs until the next question or
    heading. A capitalized line that does not end like a sentence opens a
    section, but only outside a question or after a blank line, so a
    wrapped question keeps its second line. Sections left without
    questions are dropped.

    Args:
        text (str): The source text.
        title (str | None): Overrides the title line found in the text.
        subtitle (str | None): Overrides the subtitle line found in the
            text.
        vocabulary (AnswerKeyVocabulary): Markers to recognize and labels
            to print. English by default.
        max_chars (int | None): Longest accepted source, in characters;
            ``None`` accepts any length.

    Returns:
        AnswerKey: The answer key. Its title falls back, in order, to the
        title line, the first section's heading and the vocabulary's
        ``default_title``.

    Raises:
        SlideSourceEmptyError: If ``text`` is empty or whitespace.
        SlideSourceTooLargeError: If ``text`` is longer than ``max_chars``.
    """
    _check_source(text, max_chars)
    reader = _AnswerKeyReader(vocabulary)
    reader.read(text)
    first_heading = reader.sections[0].title if reader.sections else ""
    return AnswerKey(
        title=title or reader.title or first_heading or vocabulary.default_title,
        subtitle=subtitle or reader.subtitle,
        sections=[section for section in reader.sections if section.items],
    )

    DEFAULT_MAX_SOURCE_CHARS: int = 200000

    Longest source text accepted, in characters. Ported from the MAX_TEXT_LENGTH default of Leviathan's slide-generator.

    def __init__(
    self,
    *,
    vocabulary: SlideVocabulary = DEFAULT_SLIDE_VOCABULARY,
    max_concurrent: int = DEFAULT_MAX_CONCURRENT_RENDERS,
) -> None:
    """Configure the renderer.

    Args:
        vocabulary (SlideVocabulary): Labels printed on the slides —
            pass the one the deck was parsed with.
        max_concurrent (int): PDF, PPTX and DOCX renders allowed at
            once.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``max_concurrent`` is below 1.
    """
    if max_concurrent < 1:
        raise ValueError("max_concurrent must be >= 1")
    self.vocabulary: SlideVocabulary = vocabulary
    self._semaphore: asyncio.Semaphore = asyncio.Semaphore(max_concurrent)
    self._pdf: PdfRenderer = PdfRenderer(max_concurrent=max_concurrent)

    async def pdf(
    self, deck: SlideDeck, *, theme: SlideThemeEnum = SlideThemeEnum.DEFAULT
) -> bytes:
    """Render the deck as a PDF, one 1280x720 page per slide.

    Args:
        deck (SlideDeck): The deck.
        theme (SlideThemeEnum): Colour scheme.

    Returns:
        bytes: The PDF.

    Raises:
        ImportError: When the ``[slides]`` extra is missing.
    """
    async with self._semaphore:
        try:
            return await self._pdf.render_html(self.html(deck, theme=theme))
        except ImportError as exc:  # pragma: no cover - extra-gated
            raise ImportError(missing_extra_message("weasyprint")) from exc

    SlideVocabulary dataclass ¶

    SlideVocabulary(
    lesson_pattern: str = "^Lesson\\s+(\\d+)\\s*:\\s*(.+?)\\s*$",
    notes_pattern: str = "^(?:Notes|Note)\\s*:\\s*(.+)$",
    conclusion_marker: str = "conclusion",
    sentence_verbs: tuple[str, ...] = DEFAULT_SENTENCE_VERBS,
    ignored_lines: frozenset[str] = frozenset(),
    default_lesson_title: str = "Content",
    default_deck_title: str = "Slides",
    lesson_label: str = "Lesson {index}",
    conclusion_label: str = "Conclusion",
    handout_subtitle: str = "Presenter handout",
    handout_cover_note: str = "Cover slide.",
    notes_heading: str = "Speaker notes",
    slide_label: str = "Slide",
    language: str = "en",
)

    Markers the slide parser reads and labels the slide renderers print.

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    lesson_pattern str

    Regular expression matching a lesson header, case-insensitive, with group 1 the lesson number and group 2 its title.
    notes_pattern str

    Regular expression matching a speaker-notes line, case-insensitive, with group 1 the note text. The note attaches to the paragraph or bullet right above it.
    conclusion_marker str

    Lowercase fragment that, found in a section title, renders that section as a conclusion slide.
    sentence_verbs tuple[str, ...]

    Space-padded verbs whose presence in a Head: tail head means the line is prose.
    ignored_lines frozenset[str]

    Lowercase lines dropped wherever they appear — the button labels and watermarks text copied from a web page carries along.
    default_lesson_title str

    Title of the implicit lesson created when content appears before any lesson header.
    default_deck_title str

    Deck title when the text has no lesson header and the caller passed none.
    lesson_label str

    Eyebrow of a lesson's slides; {index} is the lesson number.
    conclusion_label str

    Eyebrow of a conclusion slide.
    handout_subtitle str

)

    Verbs that mark a Head: tail line as a sentence, not a bullet.

    def __init__(
    self,
    *,
    stylesheet: str = DEFAULT_MARKDOWN_CSS,
    max_chars: int | None = DEFAULT_MAX_SOURCE_CHARS,
    max_archive_bytes: int = DEFAULT_MAX_ARCHIVE_BYTES,
    max_archive_members: int = DEFAULT_MAX_ARCHIVE_MEMBERS,
    mermaid_timeout: float = DEFAULT_MERMAID_TIMEOUT,
    mermaid_error_message: str = DEFAULT_MERMAID_ERROR,
    default_title: str = DEFAULT_DOCUMENT_TITLE,
    max_concurrent: int = DEFAULT_MAX_CONCURRENT_RENDERS,
) -> None:
    """Configure the renderer.

    Args:
        stylesheet (str): CSS inlined into every document.
        max_chars (int | None): Longest Markdown accepted, in
            characters; ``None`` accepts any length.
        max_archive_bytes (int): Largest total uncompressed size an
            archive may declare.
        max_archive_members (int): Most entries an archive may hold.
        mermaid_timeout (float): Seconds each Mermaid diagram has.
        mermaid_error_message (str): Sentence printed in place of a
            diagram that did not render.
        default_title (str): Title of a raw document rendered without
            one.
        max_concurrent (int): Documents laid out at once.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``max_concurrent`` is below 1.
    """
    if max_concurrent < 1:
        raise ValueError("max_concurrent must be >= 1")
    self.stylesheet: str = stylesheet
    self.max_chars: int | None = max_chars
    self.max_archive_bytes: int = max_archive_bytes
    self.max_archive_members: int = max_archive_members
    self.mermaid_timeout: float = mermaid_timeout
    self.mermaid_error_message: str = mermaid_error_message
    self.default_title: str = default_title
    self._semaphore: asyncio.Semaphore = asyncio.Semaphore(max_concurrent)
    self._pdf: PdfRenderer = PdfRenderer(max_concurrent=max_concurrent)

    async def render(
    self,
    text: str,
    *,
    title: str | None = None,
    render_mermaid: bool = False,
) -> MarkdownPdf:
    """Render Markdown text to PDF.

    Args:
        text (str): The Markdown.
        title (str | None): Document title; ``default_title`` when
            omitted.
        render_mermaid (bool): Whether to draw ```` ```mermaid ````
            blocks (needs ``[slides-mermaid]`` and Chromium).

    Returns:
        MarkdownPdf: The PDF and the title used.

    Raises:
        SlideSourceEmptyError: If the text is empty or whitespace.
        SlideSourceTooLargeError: If the text exceeds ``max_chars``.
        AssetRefused: If the Markdown references any URL — raw text
            has no directory to resolve against. ``details`` carries
            only ``refused_count``, never the URLs.
        ImportError: When the ``[slides]`` extra is missing.
    """
    effective_title = title or self.default_title
    html_document = await self._document(text, effective_title, render_mermaid)
    async with self._semaphore:
        content = await _without_echo(self._pdf, html_document, base_url=None)
    return MarkdownPdf(content=content, title=effective_title)

    async def render_archive(
    self,
    data: bytes,
    *,
    title: str | None = None,
    render_mermaid: bool = False,
) -> MarkdownPdf:
    """Render a zip holding one Markdown file and the images it references.

    The first ``.md`` file in path order is the document; relative
    image paths resolve against its directory, and nothing outside the
    extracted archive can be read.

    Args:
        data (bytes): The zip archive.
        title (str | None): Document title; the Markdown file's name
            without extension when omitted.
        render_mermaid (bool): Whether to draw ```` ```mermaid ````
            blocks.

    Returns:
        MarkdownPdf: The PDF and the title used.

    Raises:
        MarkdownArchiveError: If the archive is not a zip, holds an
            entry that would land outside the extraction directory, is
            too large or has too many entries, has no ``.md`` file, or
            its Markdown is not UTF-8.
        SlideSourceEmptyError: If the Markdown file is empty.
        SlideSourceTooLargeError: If the Markdown exceeds ``max_chars``.
        AssetRefused: If the Markdown references a URL outside the
            archive. ``details`` carries only ``refused_count``.
    """
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="tempest-md-") as scratch:
        root = Path(scratch).resolve()
        markdown_path = await asyncio.to_thread(self._extract, data, root)
        try:
            text = markdown_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:
            raise MarkdownArchiveError("not_utf8") from exc
        effective_title = title or markdown_path.stem
        html_document = await self._document(text, effective_title, render_mermaid)
        renderer = PdfRenderer(
            assets=AssetPolicy(allow_dirs=(root,)), max_concurrent=1
        )
        async with self._semaphore:
            content = await _without_echo(
                renderer,
                html_document,
                base_url=markdown_path.parent.as_uri() + "/",
            )
    return MarkdownPdf(content=content, title=effective_title)

    def __init__(
    self,
    message: str | None = None,
    *,
    code: str | None = None,
    status_code: int | None = None,
    details: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    headers: dict[str, str] | None = None,
    message_key: str | None = None,
    message_params: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    field: str | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Initialize the exception.

    Args:
        message (str | None): Override the class-level message. Used
            verbatim as ``detail`` when no catalog localizes it.
        code (str | None): Override the class-level error code on
            this instance only — leaves other instances of the
            same class untouched.
        status_code (int | None): Override the class-level HTTP
            status code on this instance only.
        details (dict[str, Any] | None): Structured context to
            attach to the JSON response.
        headers (dict[str, str] | None): Optional HTTP headers
            to include in the response.
        message_key (str | None): Catalog key to localize against.
            Defaults to the class-level ``message_key`` (and, at
            resolution time, to ``code`` when both are ``None``).
        message_params (dict[str, Any] | None): Values interpolated
            into the localized message template.
        field (str | None): Name of the input this failure is about
            — the form control a client should highlight. Defaults
            to the class-level ``field``. Left ``None``, the key is
            absent from the response body. Never name a field on an
            invalid-credentials failure: it leaks which half of the
            pair was right.
    """
    cls = type(self)
    self.code: str = code if code is not None else cls.code
    self.message_key: str | None = (
        message_key if message_key is not None else cls.message_key
    )
    self.message_params: dict[str, Any] = message_params or {}
    self.field: str | None = field if field is not None else cls.field
    effective_status: int = (
        status_code if status_code is not None else cls.status_code
    )
    self.details: dict[str, Any] = details or {}
    self.message: str = message or cls.message
    super().__init__(
        status_code=effective_status,
        detail=self.message,
        headers=headers,
    )

    Privacidade (LGPD)¶

    tempest_fastapi_sdk.privacy¶

    privacy ¶

    Data-subject export and erasure (LGPD art. 18, GDPR art. 15/17).

    Two halves, one per place personal data lives:

    • :class:SubjectGraph derives, from SQLAlchemy MetaData, the tables a delete of the subject's root row cascades to, exports one subject's rows without secret columns, and lists the foreign keys that would break erasure (:func:~tempest_fastapi_sdk.testing.assert_subject_graph_valid turns that into a CI guard);
    • :class:SubjectObjectStorage keeps every object of a subject under one prefix of an :class:~tempest_fastapi_sdk.storage.AsyncMinIOClient and erases the prefix in S3 batch deletes.

    SubjectGraph needs only SQLAlchemy (base install). SubjectObjectStorage needs a client, which needs the [minio] extra; importing this package does not.

    DEFAULT_SECRET_MARKERS module-attribute ¶

    DEFAULT_SECRET_MARKERS: tuple[str, ...] = ('hash', 'secret', 'password')

    Substrings that mark a column as secret by name (case-insensitive).

    A column whose name contains any of them (password_hash, totp_secret, api_key_hash) is left out of :meth:SubjectGraph.export. Mark a column explicitly with mapped_column(..., info={"secret": True}) or list it in secret_columns when the name says nothing.

    SECRET_INFO_KEY module-attribute ¶

    SECRET_INFO_KEY: str = 'secret'

    Key of Column.info that marks a column as secret when truthy.

    def __init__(
    self,
    metadata: MetaData,
    *,
    root: str | Table,
    retained: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
    secret_columns: Mapping[str, Collection[str]] | None = None,
    secret_markers: Collection[str] = DEFAULT_SECRET_MARKERS,
    exclude_binary: bool = True,
    value_matches: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Derive the closure from ``metadata``.

    Args:
        metadata (MetaData): Metadata holding every table of the
            service (``Base.metadata``).
        root (str | Table): The subject's root table, by name or object.
            Its single-column primary key is the subject id.
        retained (Mapping[str, str] | None): Foreign keys that may point
            into the closure with ``ON DELETE SET NULL`` because the row
            is kept after erasure (an invoice the tax law requires, a
            message in a shared thread). Keys are ``"table.column"``
            (``"table.col_a,col_b"`` for a composite key), values are
            the reason. Every entry must name an existing nullable
            ``SET NULL`` key into the closure, or it is reported by
            :meth:`violations`.
        secret_columns (Mapping[str, Collection[str]] | None): Columns
            to leave out of the export per table name, beyond the ones
            caught by ``secret_markers`` and ``info={"secret": True}``.
        secret_markers (Collection[str]): Case-insensitive substrings of
            a column name that mark it as secret. Defaults to
            :data:`DEFAULT_SECRET_MARKERS`.
        exclude_binary (bool): Leave ``LargeBinary`` columns (and its
            subclasses) out of the export. A queue payload or a model
            blob is not data the subject can read, and in base64 it is
            only volume. ``False`` keeps them, base64-encoded.
        value_matches (Mapping[str, str] | None): Columns that identify
            the subject **by value** rather than by foreign key — an
            invite sent *to* the subject keeps their e-mail in
            ``invites.to_email`` while its key points at the sender.
            Keys are ``"table.column"`` of a closure table, values are
            the key of the ``values`` mapping that :meth:`condition`,
            :meth:`export`, :meth:`count` and :meth:`erase` receive
            (``{"invites.to_email": "email"}`` with
            ``values={"email": "ana@example.com"}``). An entry outside
            the closure or naming a missing column is reported by
            :meth:`violations`.

    Raises:
        KeyError: When ``root`` names a table missing from ``metadata``.
        ValueError: When the root table does not have exactly one
            primary-key column.
    """
    self.metadata: MetaData = metadata
    self.root: Table = metadata.tables[root] if isinstance(root, str) else root
    primary_key = list(self.root.primary_key.columns)
    if len(primary_key) != 1:
        raise ValueError(
            f"root table {self.root.name!r} must have exactly one "
            f"primary-key column, found {len(primary_key)}"
        )
    self.retained: dict[str, str] = dict(retained or {})
    self.secret_columns: dict[str, frozenset[str]] = {
        table: frozenset(columns)
        for table, columns in (secret_columns or {}).items()
    }
    self.secret_markers: tuple[str, ...] = tuple(
        marker.lower() for marker in secret_markers
    )
    self.exclude_binary: bool = exclude_binary
    self.value_matches: dict[str, str] = dict(value_matches or {})
    self._order: list[Table] = self._closure()
    self._members: frozenset[str] = frozenset(t.name for t in self._order)

    def violations(self) -> list[str]:
    """List every foreign key that would break erasure of a subject.

    A foreign key whose target table is in the closure must cascade, or
    be a nullable ``SET NULL`` key listed in ``retained``. Anything else
    (``NO ACTION``, ``RESTRICT``, an unlisted ``SET NULL``) makes the
    root delete fail or leaves the subject's id behind. Stale
    ``retained`` entries are reported too, so the allowlist cannot rot.

    Returns:
        list[str]: One human-readable line per problem, sorted. Empty
        list when the schema supports erasure.
    """
    problems: list[str] = []
    matched: set[str] = set()
    for table in self.metadata.tables.values():
        for constraint in table.foreign_key_constraints:
            target = constraint.referred_table
            if target.name not in self._members:
                continue
            action = _ondelete(constraint)
            label = _fk_label(constraint)
            arrow = f"{label} -> {target.name}"
            if action == "CASCADE":
                continue
            if action == "SET NULL" and label in self.retained:
                matched.add(label)
                if not all(column.nullable for column in constraint.columns):
                    problems.append(
                        f"{arrow}: ON DELETE SET NULL on a NOT NULL column"
                    )
                continue
            if label in self.retained:
                matched.add(label)
                problems.append(
                    f"{arrow}: listed in retained but ON DELETE is "
                    f"{action}, expected SET NULL"
                )
                continue
            problems.append(
                f"{arrow}: ON DELETE {action} (expected CASCADE, or "
                f"SET NULL listed in retained)"
            )
    for label in sorted(set(self.retained) - matched):
        problems.append(
            f"{label}: listed in retained but no foreign key from it "
            f"points into the subject closure"
        )
    for label in sorted(self.value_matches):
        table_name, _, column_name = label.partition(".")
        if table_name not in self._members:
            problems.append(
                f"{label}: listed in value_matches but {table_name!r} is "
                f"not in the subject closure"
            )
        elif column_name not in self.metadata.tables[table_name].columns:
            problems.append(
                f"{label}: listed in value_matches but {table_name!r} has "
                f"no column {column_name!r}"
            )
    return sorted(problems)

    def is_secret(self, table: Table, column_name: str) -> bool:
    """Tell whether a column is left out of the export.

    Args:
        table (Table): The table owning the column.
        column_name (str): The column name.

    Returns:
        bool: ``True`` when the column is listed in ``secret_columns``,
        carries ``info={"secret": True}``, its name contains one of
        ``secret_markers``, or — under ``exclude_binary`` — its type is
        ``LargeBinary``.
    """
    if column_name in self.secret_columns.get(table.name, frozenset()):
        return True
    column = table.columns[column_name]
    if column.info.get(SECRET_INFO_KEY):
        return True
    if self.exclude_binary and isinstance(column.type, LargeBinary):
        return True
    lowered = column_name.lower()
    return any(marker in lowered for marker in self.secret_markers)

    def exported_columns(self, table: str | Table) -> list[str]:
    """Return the columns of a closure table that the export includes.

    Args:
        table (str | Table): A table of the closure, by name or object.

    Returns:
        list[str]: Column names in declaration order, secrets removed.

    Raises:
        KeyError: When the table is not part of the closure.
    """
    resolved = self._member(table)
    return [
        column.name
        for column in resolved.columns
        if not self.is_secret(resolved, column.name)
    ]

    def condition(
    self,
    table: str | Table,
    subject_id: Any,
    *,
    values: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
) -> ColumnElement[bool]:
    """Build the ``WHERE`` clause selecting one subject's rows of a table.

    The root matches on its primary key. Any other table matches when
    one of its cascading foreign keys points at a row of a closure table
    that itself belongs to the subject, as a nested ``IN (SELECT ...)``.
    A row reachable only through a cycle back to its own table (a reply
    to a reply, by another subject) is not considered the subject's.
    A table listed in ``value_matches`` also matches when its column
    equals the given value, and so do the rows that cascade from it.

    Args:
        table (str | Table): A table of the closure.
        subject_id (Any): The value of the root's primary key.
        values (Mapping[str, Any] | None): The subject's identifying
            values, by the keys ``value_matches`` names. A key left out
            (or ``None``) adds no match.

    Returns:
        ColumnElement[bool]: The clause, usable in ``select``,
        ``update`` or ``delete``.

    Raises:
        KeyError: When the table is not part of the closure.
    """
    return self._condition(
        self._member(table), subject_id, frozenset(), dict(values or {})
    )

    async def export(
    self,
    session: AsyncSession,
    subject_id: Any,
    *,
    values: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
) -> dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]]:
    """Read every row of the closure that belongs to one subject.

    Args:
        session (AsyncSession): An open async session.
        subject_id (Any): The value of the root's primary key.
        values (Mapping[str, Any] | None): The subject's identifying
            values, for the tables in ``value_matches``.

    Returns:
        dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]]: Every closure table name (in
        :meth:`tables` order) mapped to its rows, each row a dict of the
        :meth:`exported_columns` with JSON-serialisable values. A table
        with no rows maps to an empty list; an unknown subject yields
        empty lists throughout.
    """
    payload: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]] = {}
    for table in self._order:
        columns = [table.columns[name] for name in self.exported_columns(table)]
        statement = select(*columns).where(
            self._condition(table, subject_id, frozenset(), dict(values or {}))
        )
        result = await session.execute(statement)
        payload[table.name] = [
            {key: _jsonable(value) for key, value in row.items()}
            for row in result.mappings()
        ]
    return payload

    async def count(
    self,
    session: AsyncSession,
    subject_id: Any,
    *,
    values: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
) -> dict[str, int]:
    """Count one subject's rows per closure table.

    Run it after deleting the root row to prove the erasure reached
    every table: every count must be ``0``. Pass the same ``values``
    as the export — without them, a row the subject owns only by value
    is not counted, and the proof says ``0`` with it still stored.

    Args:
        session (AsyncSession): An open async session.
        subject_id (Any): The value of the root's primary key.
        values (Mapping[str, Any] | None): The subject's identifying
            values, for the tables in ``value_matches``.

    Returns:
        dict[str, int]: Every closure table name mapped to its row
        count for the subject.
    """
    counts: dict[str, int] = {}
    for table in self._order:
        statement = (
            select(func.count())
            .select_from(table)
            .where(
                self._condition(table, subject_id, frozenset(), dict(values or {}))
            )
        )
        counts[table.name] = int((await session.execute(statement)).scalar_one())
    return counts

    async def erase(
    self,
    session: AsyncSession,
    subject_id: Any,
    *,
    values: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
) -> dict[str, int]:
    """Delete one subject's rows and return the proof.

    Deletes the rows each ``value_matches`` entry selects (the database
    cascades from them), then the root row (the database cascades the
    rest of the closure), flushes, and returns :meth:`count` — which
    should be ``0`` everywhere. It does not commit: the caller decides,
    and can roll back when the proof is not clean.

    Args:
        session (AsyncSession): An open async session. The ``ON DELETE``
            rules must be enforced by the connection (on SQLite, with
            foreign keys on, which the SDK's engines turn on).
        subject_id (Any): The value of the root's primary key.
        values (Mapping[str, Any] | None): The subject's identifying
            values, for the tables in ``value_matches``.

    Returns:
        dict[str, int]: :meth:`count` after the deletes.
    """
    given = dict(values or {})
    for table in reversed(self._order):
        clauses = self._value_clauses(table, given)
        if clauses:
            await session.execute(delete(table).where(or_(*clauses)))
    primary_key = next(iter(self.root.primary_key.columns))
    await session.execute(delete(self.root).where(primary_key == subject_id))
    await session.flush()
    return await self.count(session, subject_id, values=given)

    def __init__(self, subject_id: str, errors: list[ObjectDeleteError]) -> None:
    """Build the error.

    Args:
        subject_id (str): The subject whose prefix was being erased.
        errors (list[ObjectDeleteError]): The keys the store refused.
    """
    self.subject_id: str = subject_id
    self.errors: list[ObjectDeleteError] = errors
    sample = ", ".join(f"{e.key} ({e.code})" for e in errors[:5])
    super().__init__(
        f"{len(errors)} object(s) of subject {subject_id!r} were not "
        f"deleted: {sample}"
    )

    def __init__(
    self,
    client: SubjectStorageClient,
    *,
    prefix: str = "subjects",
    bucket: str | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Wrap ``client``.

    Args:
        client (SubjectStorageClient): The object-storage client.
        prefix (str): Root prefix every subject lives under. Leading and
            trailing slashes are stripped; inner slashes are allowed
            (``"tenants/acme/users"``). Default ``"subjects"``.
        bucket (str | None): Bucket for every operation; ``None`` uses
            the client's ``default_bucket``.

    Raises:
        ValueError: When ``prefix`` is empty after stripping slashes or
            holds an empty, ``.`` or ``..`` segment.
    """
    cleaned = prefix.strip("/")
    for part in cleaned.split("/"):
        _segment(part, "prefix segment")
    self.client: SubjectStorageClient = client
    self.prefix: str = cleaned
    self.bucket: str | None = bucket

    def key(self, subject_id: object, name: str) -> str:
    """Return the full object key of one subject's object.

    Args:
        subject_id (object): The subject id; converted with ``str()``.
        name (str): Object name relative to the subject's prefix. Inner
            slashes are allowed (``"exports/2026.zip"``).

    Returns:
        str: ``"<prefix>/<subject_id>/<name>"``.

    Raises:
        ValueError: When the subject id is not a valid segment, or
            ``name`` is empty, starts with ``/``, or holds an empty,
            ``.`` or ``..`` segment — anything that could step outside
            the subject's prefix.

    for part in name.split("/"):
        _segment(part, "name segment")
    return f"{self.subject_prefix(subject_id)}{name}"

    async def put(
    self,
    subject_id: object,
    name: str,
    data: bytes | BinaryIO,
    *,
    content_type: str = "application/octet-stream",
    metadata: dict[str, str] | None = None,
    length: int | None = None,
) -> str:
    """Upload an object under the subject's prefix.

    Args:
        subject_id (object): The subject id.
        name (str): Object name relative to the subject's prefix.
        data (bytes | BinaryIO): Payload; file-like data needs
            ``length`` (``-1`` for unknown-length multipart).
        content_type (str): MIME type.
        metadata (dict[str, str] | None): User metadata.
        length (int | None): Payload size for file-like data.

    Returns:
        str: The full object key written.

    Raises:
        ValueError: When the subject id or name is invalid, or file-like
            data omits ``length``.
        S3Error: When the upload fails.
    """
    key = self.key(subject_id, name)
    await self.client.put_object(
        key,
        data,
        bucket=self.bucket,
        content_type=content_type,
        metadata=metadata,
        length=length,
    )
    return key

    async def presign(
    self,
    subject_id: object,
    name: str,
    *,
    expires: timedelta = timedelta(hours=1),
    filename: str | None = None,
    media_type: str | None = None,

) -> str:
    """Generate a temporary download URL for one subject's object.

    Pass ``media_type`` with the type the server checked — from

    link answers with it: S3 signs it as a ``response-content-type``
    override, the local backend binds it into its signature.

        subject_id (object): The subject id.
        name (str): Object name relative to the subject's prefix.

        bucket=self.bucket,
        expires=expires,
        filename=filename,
        media_type=media_type,
        as_attachment=as_attachment,

    async def read(
    self,
    subject_id: object,
    name: str,
    *,
    max_bytes: int | None = None,
) -> bytes:
    """Read one subject's object into memory, optionally capped.

    With ``max_bytes``, only the first ``max_bytes`` bytes are requested
    from the store (a ``Range`` read through
    :meth:`~tempest_fastapi_sdk.storage.AsyncMinIOClient.stream_object`),
    and reading stops there even if the store answers with more. An
    object that was swapped for a larger one after a :meth:`stat` never
    enters memory whole.

    To detect "too large", pass ``limit + 1`` and compare the length:
    ``len(data) > limit`` means the object exceeds ``limit``, without
    reading the rest of it.

    Args:
        subject_id (object): The subject id.
        name (str): Object name relative to the subject's prefix.
        max_bytes (int | None): Read at most this many bytes. ``None``
            (default) reads the whole object.

    Returns:
        bytes: The object's bytes, or its first ``max_bytes`` bytes.

    Raises:
        ValueError: When the subject id or name is invalid, or
            ``max_bytes`` is not positive.
        S3Error: When the object is missing or the request fails;
            propagated unchanged from the client
            (``FakeObjectStorageClient`` raises
            :class:`FileNotFoundError` instead).
        IntegrationDisabledException: When the client was built with
            ``enabled=False``.
    """
    if max_bytes is not None and max_bytes < 1:
        raise ValueError(f"max_bytes must be at least 1, got {max_bytes}")
    stream = await self.client.stream_object(
        self.key(subject_id, name),
        bucket=self.bucket,
        length=max_bytes,
    )
    buffer = bytearray()
    async for chunk in stream:
        buffer.extend(chunk)
        if max_bytes is not None and len(buffer) >= max_bytes:
            break
    if max_bytes is not None:
        del buffer[max_bytes:]
    return bytes(buffer)

    async def names(self, subject_id: object) -> list[str]:
    """List every object name of a subject.

    Args:
        subject_id (object): The subject id.

    Returns:
        list[str]: Names relative to the subject's prefix, sorted. Empty
        list when the subject has no objects.

    Raises:
        ValueError: When the subject id is invalid.
    """
    prefix = self.subject_prefix(subject_id)
    keys = await self.client.list_objects(prefix, bucket=self.bucket)
    return sorted(key.removeprefix(prefix) for key in keys)

    async def delete_all(self, subject_id: object) -> int:
    """Erase every object under the subject's prefix.

    Lists the prefix and removes the keys with
    :meth:`~tempest_fastapi_sdk.storage.AsyncMinIOClient.remove_objects`
    (one S3 ``DeleteObjects`` request per 1000 keys). Objects of other
    subjects are never listed, so never deleted. Calling it again is a
    no-op that returns ``0``.

    Args:
        subject_id (object): The subject id.

    Returns:
        int: Number of objects deleted.

    Raises:
        ValueError: When the subject id is invalid.
        SubjectErasureError: When the store refused to delete some keys;
            the others are deleted.
    """
    prefix = self.subject_prefix(subject_id)
    keys = await self.client.list_objects(prefix, bucket=self.bucket)
    if not keys:
        return 0
    errors = await self.client.remove_objects(keys, bucket=self.bucket)
    if errors:
        raise SubjectErasureError(str(subject_id), errors)
    return len(keys)

    SubjectStorageClient ¶

    Bases: Protocol

    The object-storage calls :class:SubjectObjectStorage makes.

    :class:~tempest_fastapi_sdk.storage.AsyncMinIOClient satisfies it, and so does :class:~tempest_fastapi_sdk.testing.fakes.FakeObjectStorageClient, which is what lets a test build the storage without MinIO. The signatures are AsyncMinIOClient's, minus the keyword arguments the storage never passes.

    tempest_fastapi_sdk.artifacts¶

    ArtifactVersionMixin ¶

    Bases: _MixinBase

    Columns for a versioned, activatable binary artifact.

    Mix into a concrete BaseModel table so an artifact name can hold many versions with exactly one is_current per name.

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    name str

    Indexed logical artifact key. Many versions share one name; the manifest resolves the current one per name.
    version str

    Opaque, human-facing version label (e.g. "1.2.0" or a build hash). Not parsed or ordered by the SDK.
    file_key str

    Object-storage key of the uploaded bytes. Immutable once written — checksums are derived from it on demand and memoized by this key.
    is_current bool

    Whether this row is the version currently served for its name. Defaults to False; exactly one row per name should be True (enforced by the activate action, not a DB constraint).

    async def activate(self, version_id: UUID) -> TModel:
    """Make one version the current one for its name.

    Flips ``is_current`` on the selected row and clears it on every
    sibling of the same ``name`` in a single transaction, so exactly
    one version per name is ever current.

    Args:
        version_id (UUID): Primary key of the version to activate.

    Returns:
        TModel: The activated row (refreshed).

    Raises:
        AppException: The repository's ``not_found_exception`` when
            no version with ``version_id`` exists.
    """
    target = await self.repository.get_by_id(version_id)
    model = self.repository.model
    session = self.repository.session
    await session.execute(
        update(model).where(model.name == target.name).values(is_current=False),
    )
    target.is_current = True
    await session.commit()
    await session.refresh(target)
    return target

    async def build_manifest_entries[TModel: ArtifactVersionMixin](
    registry: ArtifactRegistry[TModel],
    *,
    digest_source: Callable[[TModel], Awaitable[tuple[str, int]]],
) -> list[ArtifactManifestEntry]:
    """Build manifest entries from a registry's current rows.

    Stays serialization-agnostic: it resolves the current version of
    every artifact and asks ``digest_source`` for each row's ``(sha256,
    size)``. The caller's ``digest_source`` decides where the bytes come
    from — typically
    :func:`~tempest_fastapi_sdk.artifacts.object_digest` against MinIO,
    with a :func:`~tempest_fastapi_sdk.artifacts.file_digest` fallback to
    a bundled on-disk file.

    Args:
        registry (ArtifactRegistry[TModel]): The registry to read current
            rows from.
        digest_source (Callable[[TModel], Awaitable[tuple[str, int]]]):
            Async function mapping a current row to its ``(sha256,
            size)``.

    Returns:
        list[ArtifactManifestEntry]: One entry per current artifact
        (``[]`` when nothing has been activated).
    """
    entries: list[ArtifactManifestEntry] = []
    for row in await registry.list_current():
        sha256, size = await digest_source(row)
        entries.append(
            ArtifactManifestEntry(
                name=row.name,
                version=row.version,
                file_key=row.file_key,
                sha256=sha256,
                size=size,
            ),
        )
    return entries

    async def file_digest(path: str | Path) -> tuple[str, int]:
    """Return the streamed ``(sha256, size)`` of an on-disk file, memoized.

    The file read runs in a worker thread (``asyncio.to_thread``) so the
    event loop stays responsive; the result is cached by the resolved
    path string, so repeat calls never re-read the file.

    Args:
        path (str | Path): Path to the file to digest.

    Returns:
        tuple[str, int]: The hex SHA-256 and the size in bytes.
    """
    key = str(path)
    cached = _file_cache.get(key)
    if cached is None:
        cached = await asyncio.to_thread(_read_file_digest, Path(path))
        _file_cache[key] = cached
    return cached

    async def object_digest(
    client: AsyncMinIOClient,
    bucket: str,
    key: str,
) -> tuple[str, int]:
    """Return the streamed ``(sha256, size)`` of a stored object, memoized.

    Streams the object from MinIO/S3 chunk by chunk (never loading the
    whole payload into memory) and caches the result by ``(bucket,
    key)`` — safe because an object key is immutable for its content.

    Args:
        client (AsyncMinIOClient): The object-storage client.
        bucket (str): The bucket the object lives in.
        key (str): The object key.

    Returns:
        tuple[str, int]: The hex SHA-256 and the size in bytes.
    """
    cache_key = (bucket, key)
    cached = _object_cache.get(cache_key)
    if cached is None:
        digest = hashlib.sha256()
        size = 0
        stream = await client.stream_object(key, bucket=bucket, chunk_size=_CHUNK_SIZE)
        async for chunk in stream:
            digest.update(chunk)
            size += len(chunk)
        cached = (digest.hexdigest(), size)
        _object_cache[cache_key] = cached
    return cached

    def make_activate_artifact_action(
    *,
    label: str = "Activate version",
    name: str = "activate_artifact",
    dangerous: bool = False,
) -> AdminAction:
    """Build an admin action that activates the selected artifact version.

    Register the returned action's handler on an ``AdminModel``::

        action = make_activate_artifact_action(label="Ativar versão")
        site.register(AdminModel(model=ModelVersion, actions=[action.handler]))

    Args:
        label (str): Dropdown label shown to the operator.
        name (str): Stable identifier (the submitted form value); must
            be unique among the model's actions.
        dangerous (bool): Flag the action as destructive for a stronger
            UI confirm.

    Returns:
        AdminAction: The action metadata + handler. Its ``handler``
        carries the ``@admin_action`` marker, so pass ``action.handler``
        to ``AdminModel(actions=[...])``.
    """

    @admin_action(label=label, name=name, dangerous=dangerous)
    async def _activate(ctx: AdminActionContext) -> AdminActionResult:
        """Activate the selected version, clearing same-name siblings.

        Args:
            ctx (AdminActionContext): Selected row ids + request DB
                session + repository for the admin's model.

        Returns:
            AdminActionResult: Flash message shown on the list view.
        """
        session = ctx.db_session
        model = ctx.repository.model
        rows = (
            (await session.execute(select(model).where(model.id.in_(ctx.ids))))
            .scalars()
            .all()
        )
        if len(rows) != 1:
            return AdminActionResult(
                "Select exactly one version to activate.",
                category="warning",
            )
        target = rows[0]
        await session.execute(
            update(model).where(model.name == target.name).values(is_current=False),
        )
        target.is_current = True
        await session.commit()
        return AdminActionResult(
            f"Activated version {target.version!r} of {target.name!r}.",
        )

    return resolve_admin_action(_activate)

    Compartilhamento (Open Graph)¶

    tempest_fastapi_sdk.share¶

    share ¶

    Link previews for shared items: the Open Graph page and its card image.

    A link shared on WhatsApp, Telegram, Instagram or X becomes a preview built from the Open Graph tags of the HTML the URL returns, fetched by a crawler that runs no JavaScript. :func:make_share_router serves that HTML per item, from a resolver the service writes, and — with a :class:ShareCardRenderer — the 1200x630 PNG the preview shows.

    from tempest_fastapi_sdk.share import (
    ShareCardRenderer,
    SharePreviewSchema,
    make_share_router,
)

app.include_router(
    make_share_router(
        resolve_trip,
        public_url="https://api.example.com",
        fallback=SharePreviewSchema(
            title="BusCar",
            description="Caronas entre cidades",
            redirect_url="https://app.example.com",
        ),
        renderer=ShareCardRenderer(),
    )
)

    For the image someone posts rather than the preview a link gets, :class:ShareFrameRenderer draws a frame — story or square — with a QR code in the middle, and :func:render_qr draws the QR code alone, both with the brand logo inside the code at a measured, capped size.

    The page needs nothing beyond the base install; the renderers need the [image] extra (pillow, segno) and a TrueType font on the machine (fonts-dejavu-core on Debian/Ubuntu). Importing this module needs neither: Pillow is imported when a renderer is built.

    Re-exports use the PEP 484 from x import Y as Y explicit re-export form combined with __all__ so every type-checker accepts from tempest_fastapi_sdk.share import make_share_router without a diagnostic.

    Draws share cards as 1200x630 PNG.

    Layout, top to bottom: brand (accent) with the logo at the right, kicker (muted), title (bold, shrinks from 72 to 48 px on one line, else wraps to two lines at 56 px, then is cut with …), the lines (icon in the accent color + text), the chips and the footer. Text never leaves the margins: what does not fit shrinks, is cut, or — for lines and chips — is dropped.

    Construction arguments are those of the shared base: background, text_color, muted_color, accent_color, chip_color, chip_text_color, logo, font_path and bold_font_path.

    Rendering is CPU-bound and synchronous; the share router calls :meth:render through :func:asyncio.to_thread.

    def __init__(
    self,
    *,
    background: str | tuple[str, str] = ("#0b3d91", "#061f4a"),
    text_color: str = "#ffffff",
    muted_color: str = "#c7d4f0",
    accent_color: str = "#ffd166",
    chip_color: str = "#ffffff",
    chip_text_color: str = "#0b3d91",
    logo: bytes | Path | None = None,
    font_path: Path | None = None,
    bold_font_path: Path | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Validate colors, load the fonts and decode the logo.

    Args:
        background (str | tuple[str, str]): One color, or the top and
            bottom of a vertical gradient. Any color Pillow parses
            (``"#0b3d91"``, ``"rgb(11, 61, 145)"``, ``"navy"``).
        text_color (str): Title and line text.
        muted_color (str): Kicker and footer.
        accent_color (str): Brand and line icons.
        chip_color (str): Chip fill.
        chip_text_color (str): Chip text.
        logo (bytes | Path | None): PNG/JPEG/WebP of the brand;
            transparency is kept. The card draws it at the top
            right, scaled to :data:`LOGO_HEIGHT`.
        font_path (Path | None): Regular TrueType font. ``None`` tries
            :data:`DEFAULT_FONT_CANDIDATES`.
        bold_font_path (Path | None): Bold TrueType font; ``None``
            reuses ``font_path`` (or the candidate's bold).

    Raises:
        ImportError: Without the ``[image]`` extra (Pillow).
        ValueError: When a color does not parse or the logo is not an
            image Pillow decodes.
        FileNotFoundError: When no font file is found.
    """
    try:
        from PIL import Image, ImageColor
    except ImportError as exc:
        raise ImportError(
            f"{type(self).__name__} requires the [image] extra (pillow). "
            "Install with `pip install tempest-fastapi-sdk[image]`."
        ) from exc
    top, bottom = (
        (background, background) if isinstance(background, str) else background
    )
    colors: dict[str, str] = {
        "background_top": top,
        "background_bottom": bottom,
        "text_color": text_color,
        "muted_color": muted_color,
        "accent_color": accent_color,
        "chip_color": chip_color,
        "chip_text_color": chip_text_color,
    }
    parsed: dict[str, tuple[int, int, int]] = {}
    for name, value in colors.items():
        try:
            rgb = ImageColor.getrgb(value)
        except ValueError as exc:
            raise ValueError(f"{name}: unknown color {value!r}") from exc
        parsed[name] = (rgb[0], rgb[1], rgb[2])
    self._colors: dict[str, tuple[int, int, int]] = parsed
    self._regular_path, self._bold_path = _resolve_fonts(font_path, bold_font_path)
    self._fonts: dict[tuple[bool, int], FreeTypeFont] = {}
    logo_bytes = _read_logo(logo)
    self._logo: PillowImage | None = None
    self._logo_source: PillowImage | None = None
    if logo_bytes is not None:
        try:
            with Image.open(io.BytesIO(logo_bytes)) as source:
                if source.width * source.height > MAX_LOGO_PIXELS:
                    raise ValueError("logo is larger than MAX_LOGO_PIXELS")
                image = source.convert("RGBA")
        except (OSError, Image.DecompressionBombError) as exc:
            raise ValueError(f"logo is not a decodable image: {exc}") from exc
        self._logo_source = image
        ratio = min(LOGO_HEIGHT / image.height, MAX_LOGO_WIDTH / image.width)
        self._logo = image.resize(
            (
                max(1, round(image.width * ratio)),
                max(1, round(image.height * ratio)),
            ),
            Image.Resampling.LANCZOS,
        )
    digest = hashlib.sha256()
    for name in sorted(parsed):
        digest.update(f"{name}={parsed[name]};".encode())
    for path in (self._regular_path, self._bold_path):
        digest.update(path.read_bytes())
    if logo_bytes is not None:
        digest.update(logo_bytes)
    self._fingerprint: str = digest.hexdigest()

    def render(self, card: ShareCardSchema) -> bytes:
    """Draw ``card`` as a PNG.

    The output is a pure function of the card and the renderer's
    colors, fonts and logo — same inputs, same bytes in the same
    Pillow and FreeType versions.

    Args:
        card (ShareCardSchema): What to draw.

    Returns:
        bytes: The PNG, :data:`OG_IMAGE_WIDTH` x :data:`OG_IMAGE_HEIGHT`.
    """
    from PIL import Image, ImageDraw

    width, height = self.width, self.height
    image = Image.new("RGB", (width, height))
    self._paint_background(image)
    draw = ImageDraw.Draw(image)
    usable = width - 2 * MARGIN
    header_width = usable
    if self._logo is not None:
        logo_x = width - MARGIN - self._logo.width
        image.paste(self._logo, (logo_x, 48), self._logo)
        header_width = max(0, logo_x - MARGIN - 24)
    y = 52
    if card.brand:
        brand, font = self._fit(
            draw, card.brand, bold=True, size=44, min_size=32, width=header_width
        )
        draw.text((MARGIN, y), brand, font=font, fill=self._colors["accent_color"])
        y += 64
    if card.kicker:
        kicker, font = self._fit(
            draw, card.kicker, bold=False, size=32, min_size=26, width=header_width
        )
        draw.text((MARGIN, y), kicker, font=font, fill=self._colors["muted_color"])
        y += 52
    y = max(y + 8, 140)
    title_lines, title_font = self._wrap_title(draw, card.title, usable)
    step = int(title_font.size * 1.15)
    for line in title_lines:
        draw.text(
            (MARGIN, y), line, font=title_font, fill=self._colors["text_color"]
        )
        y += step
    y += 16
    chips_top = height - 168 if card.chips else height - MARGIN
    footer_top = height - 76
    lines_bottom = min(chips_top, footer_top if card.footer else height) - 12
    icon_font = self._font(bold=True, size=34)
    icon_column = max(
        (
            int(draw.textlength(e.icon, font=icon_font))
            for e in card.lines
            if e.icon
        ),
        default=0,
    )
    for entry in card.lines:
        if not entry.text:
            continue
        if y + 44 > lines_bottom:
            break
        x = MARGIN
        if icon_column:
            draw.text(
                (x, y),
                entry.icon or "",
                font=icon_font,
                fill=self._colors["accent_color"],
            )
            x += icon_column + 16
        text, font = self._fit(
            draw,
            entry.text,
            bold=False,
            size=34,
            min_size=26,
            width=width - MARGIN - x,
        )
        draw.text((x, y), text, font=font, fill=self._colors["text_color"])
        y += 52
    if card.chips:
        x = MARGIN
        for chip in card.chips:
            right = self._chip(draw, x, chips_top, chip, width - MARGIN)
            if right is None:
                break
            x = right + 20
    if card.footer:
        footer, font = self._fit(
            draw, card.footer, bold=False, size=30, min_size=24, width=usable
        )
        draw.text(
            (MARGIN, footer_top),
            footer,
            font=font,
            fill=self._colors["muted_color"],
        )
    output = io.BytesIO()
    image.save(output, format="PNG", optimize=True)
    return output.getvalue()

    Bases: _BrandRenderer

    Draws the shareable frame as PNG, in the story or square layout.

    Top to bottom: logo and brand; the person's photo in a circle ringed in the accent color (their initials when there is no photo), title and subtitle; a white panel with the QR code of url — the brand logo in its middle when the renderer has one; the link written out; the caption. Text shrinks, then is cut with …; nothing leaves the margins.

    Construction arguments are the card's: background, text_color, muted_color, accent_color, chip_color, chip_text_color, logo, font_path and bold_font_path (the chip colors are unused here). Fonts and colors fail at construction, not at the first render.

    Rendering is CPU-bound and synchronous; call it through :func:asyncio.to_thread from a route.

    def __init__(
    self,
    *,
    background: str | tuple[str, str] = ("#0b3d91", "#061f4a"),
    text_color: str = "#ffffff",
    muted_color: str = "#c7d4f0",
    accent_color: str = "#ffd166",
    chip_color: str = "#ffffff",
    chip_text_color: str = "#0b3d91",
    logo: bytes | Path | None = None,
    font_path: Path | None = None,
    bold_font_path: Path | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Validate colors, load the fonts and decode the logo.

    Args:
        background (str | tuple[str, str]): One color, or the top and
            bottom of a vertical gradient. Any color Pillow parses
            (``"#0b3d91"``, ``"rgb(11, 61, 145)"``, ``"navy"``).
        text_color (str): Title and line text.
        muted_color (str): Kicker and footer.
        accent_color (str): Brand and line icons.
        chip_color (str): Chip fill.
        chip_text_color (str): Chip text.
        logo (bytes | Path | None): PNG/JPEG/WebP of the brand;
            transparency is kept. The card draws it at the top
            right, scaled to :data:`LOGO_HEIGHT`.
        font_path (Path | None): Regular TrueType font. ``None`` tries
            :data:`DEFAULT_FONT_CANDIDATES`.
        bold_font_path (Path | None): Bold TrueType font; ``None``
            reuses ``font_path`` (or the candidate's bold).

    Raises:
        ImportError: Without the ``[image]`` extra (Pillow).
        ValueError: When a color does not parse or the logo is not an
            image Pillow decodes.
        FileNotFoundError: When no font file is found.
    """
    try:
        from PIL import Image, ImageColor
    except ImportError as exc:
        raise ImportError(
            f"{type(self).__name__} requires the [image] extra (pillow). "
            "Install with `pip install tempest-fastapi-sdk[image]`."
        ) from exc
    top, bottom = (
        (background, background) if isinstance(background, str) else background
    )
    colors: dict[str, str] = {
        "background_top": top,
        "background_bottom": bottom,
        "text_color": text_color,
        "muted_color": muted_color,
        "accent_color": accent_color,
        "chip_color": chip_color,
        "chip_text_color": chip_text_color,
    }
    parsed: dict[str, tuple[int, int, int]] = {}
    for name, value in colors.items():
        try:
            rgb = ImageColor.getrgb(value)
        except ValueError as exc:
            raise ValueError(f"{name}: unknown color {value!r}") from exc
        parsed[name] = (rgb[0], rgb[1], rgb[2])
    self._colors: dict[str, tuple[int, int, int]] = parsed
    self._regular_path, self._bold_path = _resolve_fonts(font_path, bold_font_path)
    self._fonts: dict[tuple[bool, int], FreeTypeFont] = {}
    logo_bytes = _read_logo(logo)
    self._logo: PillowImage | None = None
    self._logo_source: PillowImage | None = None
    if logo_bytes is not None:
        try:
            with Image.open(io.BytesIO(logo_bytes)) as source:
                if source.width * source.height > MAX_LOGO_PIXELS:
                    raise ValueError("logo is larger than MAX_LOGO_PIXELS")
                image = source.convert("RGBA")
        except (OSError, Image.DecompressionBombError) as exc:
            raise ValueError(f"logo is not a decodable image: {exc}") from exc
        self._logo_source = image
        ratio = min(LOGO_HEIGHT / image.height, MAX_LOGO_WIDTH / image.width)
        self._logo = image.resize(
            (
                max(1, round(image.width * ratio)),
                max(1, round(image.height * ratio)),
            ),
            Image.Resampling.LANCZOS,
        )
    digest = hashlib.sha256()
    for name in sorted(parsed):
        digest.update(f"{name}={parsed[name]};".encode())
    for path in (self._regular_path, self._bold_path):
        digest.update(path.read_bytes())
    if logo_bytes is not None:
        digest.update(logo_bytes)
    self._fingerprint: str = digest.hexdigest()

    def render(
    self,
    frame: ShareFrameSchema,
    *,
    layout: ShareFrameLayoutEnum = ShareFrameLayoutEnum.STORY,
    photo: bytes | None = None,
    qr_logo_fraction: float = DEFAULT_QR_LOGO_FRACTION,
) -> bytes:
    """Draw ``frame`` as a PNG.

    Args:
        frame (ShareFrameSchema): What to draw.
        layout (ShareFrameLayoutEnum): Story (1080x1920) or square
            (1080x1080).
        photo (bytes | None): The person's photo; ``None`` draws the
            initials of ``frame.title``. EXIF orientation is applied.
        qr_logo_fraction (float): Side of the logo inside the QR code
            over the QR side, at most
            :data:`~tempest_fastapi_sdk.share.MAX_QR_LOGO_FRACTION`.

    Returns:
        bytes: The PNG.

    Raises:
        ImportError: Without the ``[image]`` extra (``segno``).
        ValueError: When the photo does not decode, or
            ``qr_logo_fraction`` is out of range.
    """
    _require_imaging()
    import segno
    from PIL import Image, ImageDraw

    geometry = LAYOUTS[ShareFrameLayoutEnum(layout)]
    image = Image.new("RGB", (geometry.width, geometry.height))
    self._paint_background(image)
    draw = ImageDraw.Draw(image)
    margin = geometry.margin

    x = margin
    if self._logo_source is not None:
        mark = self._logo_source.copy()
        mark.thumbnail(
            (geometry.width // 3, geometry.header_height),
            Image.Resampling.LANCZOS,
        )
        image.paste(mark, (x, geometry.header_y), mark)
        x += mark.width + 24
    if frame.brand:
        brand, font = self._fit(
            draw,
            frame.brand,
            bold=True,
            size=geometry.header_height * 2 // 3,
            min_size=24,
            width=geometry.width - margin - x,
        )
        draw.text(
            (x, geometry.header_y + geometry.header_height // 2),
            brand,
            font=font,
            fill=self._colors["accent_color"],
            anchor="lm",
        )

    disc = self._photo(photo, frame.title, geometry.photo_diameter)
    if geometry.photo_beside_title:
        image.paste(disc, (margin, geometry.people_y), disc)
        text_x = margin + geometry.photo_diameter + 32
        text_width = geometry.width - margin - text_x
        middle = geometry.people_y + geometry.photo_diameter // 2
        title, font = self._fit(
            draw,
            frame.title,
            bold=True,
            size=geometry.title_size,
            min_size=geometry.title_size * 2 // 3,
            width=text_width,
        )
        title_y = middle if frame.subtitle is None else middle - 8
        draw.text(
            (text_x, title_y),
            title,
            font=font,
            fill=self._colors["text_color"],
            anchor="lm" if frame.subtitle is None else "ld",
        )
        if frame.subtitle:
            subtitle, font = self._fit(
                draw,
                frame.subtitle,
                bold=False,
                size=geometry.subtitle_size,
                min_size=geometry.subtitle_size * 2 // 3,
                width=text_width,
            )
            draw.text(
                (text_x, middle + 8),
                subtitle,
                font=font,
                fill=self._colors["muted_color"],
                anchor="la",
            )
    else:
        image.paste(
            disc,
            ((geometry.width - geometry.photo_diameter) // 2, geometry.people_y),
            disc,
        )
        y = geometry.people_y + geometry.photo_diameter + 40
        self._centered(
            draw,
            frame.title,
            y=y,
            width=geometry.width,
            margin=margin,
            bold=True,
            size=geometry.title_size,
            color="text_color",
        )
        if frame.subtitle:
            self._centered(
                draw,
                frame.subtitle,
                y=y + geometry.title_size + 24,
                width=geometry.width,
                margin=margin,
                bold=False,
                size=geometry.subtitle_size,
                color="muted_color",
            )

    panel_x = (geometry.width - geometry.panel_size) // 2
    draw.rounded_rectangle(
        (
            panel_x,
            geometry.panel_y,
            panel_x + geometry.panel_size,
            geometry.panel_y + geometry.panel_size,
        ),
        radius=geometry.panel_size // 16,
        fill="white",
    )
    modules: int = int(
        segno.make(frame.url, error="h", micro=False).symbol_size(
            scale=1, border=0
        )[0]
    )
    scale = max(1, geometry.panel_size // (modules + 2 * QR_QUIET_ZONE_MODULES))
    code = qr_image(
        frame.url,
        logo=self._logo_source,
        logo_fraction=qr_logo_fraction,
        scale=scale,
        border=0,
    )
    image.paste(
        code,
        (
            (geometry.width - code.width) // 2,
            geometry.panel_y + (geometry.panel_size - code.height) // 2,
        ),
    )

    y = geometry.panel_y + geometry.panel_size + 28
    if frame.show_url:
        written = frame.url.split("://", 1)[1]
        self._centered(
            draw,
            written,
            y=y,
            width=geometry.width,
            margin=margin,
            bold=True,
            size=geometry.url_size,
            color="text_color",
        )
        y += geometry.url_size + 20
    if frame.caption and y + geometry.caption_size <= geometry.height - 16:
        self._centered(
            draw,
            frame.caption,
            y=y,
            width=geometry.width,
            margin=margin,
            bold=False,
            size=geometry.caption_size,
            color="muted_color",
        )
    output = io.BytesIO()
    image.save(output, format="PNG", optimize=True)
    return output.getvalue()

    ShareResolver ¶

    Bases: Protocol

    Looks up the preview of one item.

    Returns None when the item does not exist or must not be shown (deleted, private, sold out): the router answers with the fallback preview and no image. An exception propagates — a resolver failure is a bug or an outage, not an unavailable item, and swallowing it would hide both.

    ShareCardLineSchema ¶

    Bases: BaseSchema

    One information line on the card.

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    text str

    The line's text, shrunk and then cut with … when it does not fit.
    icon str | None

    A short glyph drawn before the text in the accent color ("→", "★", "✓"). Drawn with the card's font, so it must be a character that font has — a color emoji is not.

    ShareCardSchema ¶

    Bases: BaseSchema

    Content of the 1200x630 preview image.

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    title str

    The headline. Shrinks, then wraps to two lines, then is cut with ….
    brand str | None

    Small text at the top left, in the accent color (the product name).
    kicker str | None

    Muted line under the brand.
    lines list[ShareCardLineSchema]

    Information lines under the title. Lines that do not fit above the chips are dropped.
    chips list[str]

    Rounded labels near the bottom, left to right. Chips that would cross the right margin are dropped.
    footer str | None

    Muted line at the bottom.

    Every text is collapsed to one line (line breaks and repeated spaces become one space); empty chips are dropped.

    ShareFrameLayoutEnum ¶

    Bases: BaseStrEnum

    Shape of the shareable frame.

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    STORY

    1080x1920, the status/story format.
    SQUARE

    1080x1080, for a chat or a group.

    ShareFrameSchema ¶

    Bases: BaseSchema

    Content of the shareable frame: a QR code with who and what around it.

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    url str

    Absolute http/https URL the QR code encodes, usually the item's share page.
    title str

    Main line under the photo — the person's name.
    subtitle str | None

    Muted line under the title (the route).
    brand str | None

    Product name next to the logo, in the accent color.
    caption str | None

    Call to action under the link ("Escaneie e reserve").
    show_url bool

    Write the URL under the QR code, without the scheme, for whoever cannot scan.

    Every text is collapsed to one line, as on the card.

    SharePreviewSchema ¶

    Bases: BaseSchema

    What the share page says about one item.

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    title str

    og:title and the page <title>.
    description str

    og:description.
    redirect_url str

    Where a human lands — the app screen of the item. Absolute http/https.
    canonical_url str | None

    og:url and <link rel=canonical>. None uses the share page's own public URL.
    image_url str | None

    og:image. None uses the router's own og.png when it has a renderer and the preview has a card; otherwise the page goes out without an image.
    image_alt str | None

    og:image:alt; None reuses the title.
    version str | None

    Changes whenever the item's preview changes (an updated_at). Goes into the image ETag and into ?v= on the generated og:image — crawlers cache the image by URL, so a 304 alone never refreshes a preview already shared.
    card ShareCardSchema | None

    Content of the generated image.
